summary: The wizard wishes for a statue trap. C trap.c:maketrap calls mk_trap_statue and immediately creates a random living statue with its generated contents. The JavaScript wizard-wish caller reaches maketrap without the level-generation hook and skips that helper. Later, the hero activation arm is still refused before calling the already ported activate_statue_trap.

source.branch: trap.c:maketrap STATUE_TRAP arm (508-509) calls mk_trap_statue (390-418) for every creator, including objnam.c:readobjnam wizard trap wishes (3573). The C replay first differs on the source rndmonst_adj choice at zero-based step 35, then shows the created statue. Hero entry later follows trapeffect_statue_trap (2279-2292) and activate_statue_trap (908-932).
callers: objnam.c:readobjnam wizard trap wish calls trap.c:maketrap; js/objnam_readobjnam.js calls js/trap.js:maketrap without makeTrapStatue capability.
trap.c:maketrap directly calls mk_trap_statue on STATUE_TRAP; js/trap.js currently calls the helper only when a caller supplies a hook from js/mktrap.js, otherwise records note_unported.

hack.c:spoteffects -> trap.c:dotrap -> trapeffect_statue_trap(hero) -> activate_statue_trap; js/trap_effects.js preflight and hero arm refuse this path although activate_statue_trap exists in js/trap.js.
dependencies: Existing js/mktrap.js:mk_trap_statue covers much of source trap.c:mk_trap_statue but is local to level creation; make the source helper callable from trap.c:maketrap for every trap creator and preserve its monster-inventory transfer and RNG order.

mk_trap_statue consumes rndmonnum_adj, mkcorpstat, makemon, add_to_container, and weight results; confirm each source return and side effect. The C creates an additional statue even when one was wished and dropped on the same square.

trapeffect_statue_trap discards activate_statue_trap return and returns Trap_Effect_Finished; the existing js/trap.js:activate_statue_trap consumes animate_statue result and must retain pile order and uniqueness retry.
This source family shares js/trap.js and js/trap_effects.js with the separately assigned fire-trap port, so defer implementation until that worker scope is released.

evidence: Saved challenges/evaluations/20260928234726-v11.json at b8414122a83c8057895ab04b23b7f5c6876b3328 has 3 unmatched screens. The first RNG divergence is C rn2(3)=0 in makemon.c:rndmonst_adj at step 35, while JS draws rn2(5); the following screen has a C monster where JS still shows a statue.

Independent C recording challenges/cases/v11/hero-statue-trap-animates-statue.session.json has SHA-256 a6fba47c059202a851314f47e0d38ef04bbdbddc7552722d8b26193d0b47dc91; recipe challenges/cases/v11/hero-statue-trap-animates-statue.recipe.session.json wishes and drops a newt statue, wishes a statue trap, then returns to activate it.

Upstream trap.c:390-418, :508-509, :908-932, :2279-2292 and objnam.c:3573 establish the missing creation and activation paths. js/mktrap.js:416 has a level-only mk_trap_statue helper, js/trap.js:877 skips it without a hook, and js/trap_effects.js:3453 refuses the hero arm.
